title: How decades of stopping forest fires made them worse
speaker: Vox
zh: 【Vox】數十年的森林火災撲救如何讓情況變得更加嚴重（精選雙語跟讀教材）

cues.text: In the summer of 1910, the western United States ignited.
cues.en: In the summer of 1910, the western United States ignited.
cues.zh: 1910年夏天，美國西部著火了。

cues.text: A perfect blend of hot, dry weather, and hurricane force winds fed the blazes - eventually resulting
cues.en: A perfect blend of hot, dry weather, and hurricane force winds fed the blazes - eventually resulting
cues.zh: 炎熱、乾燥的天氣和颶風的完美結合助長了大火——最終導致了火災

cues.text: in a terrifying firestorm.
cues.en: in a terrifying firestorm.
cues.zh: 在一場可怕的風暴中。

cues.text: In just two days, 3 million acres burned, full towns were turned to ash, and nearly
cues.en: In just two days, 3 million acres burned, full towns were turned to ash, and nearly
cues.zh: 短短兩天內，300萬英畝土地被燒毀，整個城鎮化為灰燼，幾乎

cues.text: 90 people died.
cues.en: 90 people died.
cues.zh: 90人死亡。

cues.text: Its devastation was so dramatic that it shaped US forest policy for years to come.
cues.en: Its devastation was so dramatic that it shaped US forest policy for years to come.
cues.zh: 它的破壞如此嚴重，以至於影響了美國未來幾年的森林政策。

cues.text: Especially for one new agency.
cues.en: Especially for one new agency.
cues.zh: 尤其是對於一個新機構而言。

cues.text: After the 1910 blaze, the US Forest Service primarily focused on stopping fires.
cues.en: After the 1910 blaze, the US Forest Service primarily focused on stopping fires.
cues.zh: 1910 年火災後，美國林務局主要致力於滅火。

cues.text: And at first, they were really effective.
cues.en: And at first, they were really effective.
cues.zh: 起初，它們確實很有效。

cues.text: For decades, most accidental and natural forest fires were stopped as quickly as they began.
cues.en: For decades, most accidental and natural forest fires were stopped as quickly as they began.
cues.zh: 幾十年來，大多數意外和自然森林火災一發生很快就被制止。

cues.text: But today, we’re facing this: "Thousands of firefighters still battling dozens of fires in the west."
cues.en: But today, we’re facing this: "Thousands of firefighters still battling dozens of fires in the west."
cues.zh: 但今天，我們面臨著這樣的情況：“數千名消防員仍在西部與數十場火災作鬥爭。”

cues.text: "More than 85 thousand acres burned." "The worst wildfire season in state history."
cues.en: "More than 85 thousand acres burned." "The worst wildfire season in state history."
cues.zh: “超過85000英畝的土地被燒毀。” “該州歷史上最嚴重的野火季節。”

cues.text: Scientists are beginning to understand that decades of fire suppression has created dense
cues.en: Scientists are beginning to understand that decades of fire suppression has created dense
cues.zh: 科學家開始意識到，幾十年的滅火已經造成了密集的火災

cues.text: forests that are ready to ignite in catastrophic ways..
cues.en: forests that are ready to ignite in catastrophic ways..
cues.zh: 森林隨時可能發生災難性的火災。

cues.text: One proposed solution dates back hundreds of years:
cues.en: One proposed solution dates back hundreds of years:
cues.zh: 一項提議的解決方案可以追溯到數百年前：

cues.text: burning parts of our forests, on purpose.
cues.en: burning parts of our forests, on purpose.
cues.zh: 故意燃燒我們的部分森林。

cues.text: "So remember!
cues.en: "So remember!
cues.zh: 「所以記住！

cues.text: Only you can prevent forest fires." In 1944, the US Forest Service introduced Smokey the Bear - the goal was to educate
cues.en: Only you can prevent forest fires." In 1944, the US Forest Service introduced Smokey the Bear - the goal was to educate
cues.zh: 只有你才能預防森林火災。 」 1944 年，美國林務局引進了斯莫基熊 - 目的是為了教育人們

cues.text: the public on the dangers of forest fires.
cues.en: the public on the dangers of forest fires.
cues.zh: 向公眾宣傳森林火災的危險。

cues.text: But even before that famous campaign, the federal government had put thousands of men
cues.en: But even before that famous campaign, the federal government had put thousands of men
cues.zh: 但甚至在那次著名的競選之前，聯邦政府就已經派了數千人

cues.text: to work building fire towers and suppressing burns.
cues.en: to work building fire towers and suppressing burns.
cues.zh: 建造消防塔和抑制燒傷。

cues.text: In 1935, the Forest Service even established the “10 AM policy” - a rule that states
cues.en: In 1935, the Forest Service even established the “10 AM policy” - a rule that states
cues.zh: 1935 年，林務局甚至制定了「上午 10 點政策」——該規則規定

cues.text: all fires should be suppressed by 10am the day after they’re reported.
cues.en: all fires should be suppressed by 10am the day after they’re reported.
cues.zh: 所有火災應在收到報告後的第二天上午 10 點之前撲滅。

cues.text: This mentality that “all fire is bad” drove an entire generation’s understanding
cues.en: This mentality that “all fire is bad” drove an entire generation’s understanding
cues.zh: 這種「所有的火都是不好的」的心態推動了整個世代的認識

cues.text: of what fire means to a forest: “A tragedy that happens year after year in our great American forest areas."
cues.en: of what fire means to a forest: “A tragedy that happens year after year in our great American forest areas."
cues.zh: 火災對森林意味著什麼：“在我們偉大的美國森林地區年復一年發生的悲劇。”

cues.text: But by the 1960s, scientists realized that narrative isn’t entirely accurate.
cues.en: But by the 1960s, scientists realized that narrative isn’t entirely accurate.
cues.zh: 但到了 20 世紀 60 年代，科學家意識到這種敘述並不完全準確。

cues.text: KOLDEN: For most of the globe and particularly the forests in the western US, they actually
cues.en: KOLDEN: For most of the globe and particularly the forests in the western US, they actually
cues.zh: KOLDEN：對於全球大部分地區，特別是美國西部的森林來說，它們實際上

cues.text: evolved with fire.
cues.en: evolved with fire.
cues.zh: 隨著火的進化。

cues.text: Tree rings, soil samples, and charcoal records all show a history of fire - likely started
cues.en: Tree rings, soil samples, and charcoal records all show a history of fire - likely started
cues.zh: 年輪、土壤樣本和木炭記錄都顯示了火災的歷史——可能是從火災開始的

cues.text: by lightning strikes and other natural phenomena.
cues.en: by lightning strikes and other natural phenomena.
cues.zh: 雷擊和其他自然現象。

cues.text: And that history shows that fire isn’t always a destructive force - but an important part
cues.en: And that history shows that fire isn’t always a destructive force - but an important part
cues.zh: 歷史表明，火併不總是一種破壞性力量，而是一個重要組成部分

cues.text: of forest ecology.
cues.en: of forest ecology.
cues.zh: 森林生態學。

cues.text: KOLDEN: Fire plays a really important role where it is essentially removing a lot of
cues.en: KOLDEN: Fire plays a really important role where it is essentially removing a lot of
cues.zh: KOLDEN：火起著非常重要的作用，它基本上消除了很多

cues.text: the older, less productive material from the landscape and is creating pockets in patches
cues.en: the older, less productive material from the landscape and is creating pockets in patches
cues.zh: 景觀中較古老、生產力較低的材料正在形成斑塊

cues.text: of different ages of vegetation.
cues.en: of different ages of vegetation.
cues.zh: 不同年齡的植被。

cues.text: KOLDEN: That diversity of ages also produces a diversity of species.
cues.en: KOLDEN: That diversity of ages also produces a diversity of species.
cues.zh: KOLDEN：年齡的多樣性也產生了物種的多樣性。

cues.text: In many places, fires work as a “reset button” for the forest.
cues.en: In many places, fires work as a “reset button” for the forest.
cues.zh: 在許多地方，火災就像森林的「重啟按鈕」。

cues.text: It clears out dead brush and older materials and makes space for new growth.
cues.en: It clears out dead brush and older materials and makes space for new growth.
cues.zh: 它清除枯死的灌木叢和舊材料，為新的生長騰出空間。

cues.text: For some species, fire is even vital for reproduction.
cues.en: For some species, fire is even vital for reproduction.
cues.zh: 對某些物種來說，火對於繁殖甚至至關重要。

cues.text: For example, low burning fires dry out sequoia tree cones enough for them to open and drop seeds.
cues.en: For example, low burning fires dry out sequoia tree cones enough for them to open and drop seeds.
cues.zh: 例如，低燃燒的火會使紅杉樹球果乾燥，足以讓它們張開並掉落種子。

cues.text: At the same time, the fire clears the ground to expose fresh, nutrient rich soil which
cues.en: At the same time, the fire clears the ground to expose fresh, nutrient rich soil which
cues.zh: 同時，大火清理了地面，露出了新鮮、營養豐富的土壤，

cues.text: creates ideal conditions for seeds to germinate.
cues.en: creates ideal conditions for seeds to germinate.
cues.zh: 為種子發芽創造理想的條件。

cues.text: But aside from the ecological benefits, fires also help a forest become more resistant to
cues.en: But aside from the ecological benefits, fires also help a forest become more resistant to
cues.zh: 但除了生態效益之外，火災還可以幫助森林增強抵抗力

cues.text: high severity burns later on.
cues.en: high severity burns later on.
cues.zh: 隨後發生嚴重燒傷。

cues.text: Low burning fires clear the forest floor and lower branches from trees.
cues.en: Low burning fires clear the forest floor and lower branches from trees.
cues.zh: 低度燃燒的火焰清除了森林地面和樹枝。

cues.text: Then, if a more intense fire moves through the same area, it’s slowed by a lack of fuel.
cues.en: Then, if a more intense fire moves through the same area, it’s slowed by a lack of fuel.
cues.zh: 然後，如果同一區域發生更強烈的火災，由於缺乏燃料，火勢會減慢。

cues.text: KOLDEN: So when you get those type of patches all over the place, it becomes difficult for fire to move through that landscape again any time soon.
cues.en: KOLDEN: So when you get those type of patches all over the place, it becomes difficult for fire to move through that landscape again any time soon.
cues.zh: 科爾登：因此，當你在整個地方都出現這種型別的斑塊時，火災很快就很難再次穿過該地區。

cues.text: But decades of suppression have led to a build up of dry, dead materials in our forests
cues.en: But decades of suppression have led to a build up of dry, dead materials in our forests
cues.zh: 但數十年的鎮壓導致我們的森林中乾燥、死亡的物質不斷堆積

cues.text: so we’re long past that point of just letting all fires burn.
cues.en: so we’re long past that point of just letting all fires burn.
cues.zh: 所以我們早已超越了讓所有的火焰燃燒的階段。

cues.text: KOLDEN: We've got a forest that has not seen fire, but that it evolved with fire.
cues.en: KOLDEN: We've got a forest that has not seen fire, but that it evolved with fire.
cues.zh: 科爾登：我們有一片森林，雖然沒有經歷過火災，但它是隨著火災而演變的。

cues.text: KOLDEN: And so there's all of this build up in the forest of extra fuel.
cues.en: KOLDEN: And so there's all of this build up in the forest of extra fuel.
cues.zh: 科爾登：所以所有這些都在額外燃料的森林中累積起來。

cues.text: KOLDEN: And it is climate change exacerbating those extreme conditions.
cues.en: KOLDEN: And it is climate change exacerbating those extreme conditions.
cues.zh: 科爾登：氣候變遷加劇了這些極端條件。

cues.text: There’s just no simple reset button for a century of suppression...
cues.en: There’s just no simple reset button for a century of suppression...
cues.zh: 對於一個世紀的鎮壓來說，沒有簡單的重置按鈕...

cues.text: or a changing climate.
cues.en: or a changing climate.
cues.zh: 或氣候變遷。

cues.text: So in order to better adapt to a hotter, drier future, some are turning to a centuries old practice.
cues.en: So in order to better adapt to a hotter, drier future, some are turning to a centuries old practice.
cues.zh: 因此，為了更好地適應更炎熱、更乾燥的未來，有些人正在轉向數百年歷史的做法。

cues.text: Indigenous people have long understood the value of fire, and, for millennia before colonization,
cues.en: Indigenous people have long understood the value of fire, and, for millennia before colonization,
cues.zh: 原住民早已瞭解火的價值，並且在殖民化之前的幾千年裡，

cues.text: would burn sections of forest on purpose.
cues.en: would burn sections of forest on purpose.
cues.zh: 會故意燒毀部分森林。

cues.text: AZZUZ: We have a history of our men burning our hunting grounds.
cues.en: AZZUZ: We have a history of our men burning our hunting grounds.
cues.zh: 阿祖茲：我們有我們的人燒毀我們狩獵場的歷史。

cues.text: Women will burn to restore their food gathering sites.
cues.en: Women will burn to restore their food gathering sites.
cues.zh: 婦女們會焚燒食物以恢復她們的食物採集地點。

cues.text: So, you know, burning is just a key tool that we use as indigenous people to keep our environment healthy.
cues.en: So, you know, burning is just a key tool that we use as indigenous people to keep our environment healthy.
cues.zh: 所以，你知道，燃燒只是我們原住民用來維持環境健康的關鍵工具。

cues.text: But colonists began placing strict laws against burning as early as 1850 - criminalizing the
cues.en: But colonists began placing strict laws against burning as early as 1850 - criminalizing the
cues.zh: 但早在 1850 年，殖民者就開始製定嚴格的法律禁止焚燒——將焚燒定為犯罪行為。

cues.text: long-held practice.
cues.en: long-held practice.
cues.zh: 長期堅持的實踐。

cues.text: After the 1910 blaze, legislation against all burning only became more strict.
cues.en: After the 1910 blaze, legislation against all burning only became more strict.
cues.zh: 1910 年大火之後，禁止焚燒的立法變得更加嚴格。

cues.text: AZZUZ: Indigenous people could be shot for burning.
cues.en: AZZUZ: Indigenous people could be shot for burning.
cues.zh: 阿祖茲：原住民可能因焚燒而被槍殺。

cues.text: And now, we’re looking to them to lead the way.
cues.en: And now, we’re looking to them to lead the way.
cues.zh: 現在，我們期待他們帶路。

cues.text: Prescribed or controlled burns draw on those cultural indigenous practices.
cues.en: Prescribed or controlled burns draw on those cultural indigenous practices.
cues.zh: 規定或控制的燒傷借鑒了這些原住民文化習俗。

cues.text: AZUZZ: Most people think, oh, these guys just go out and burn whenever they want to.
cues.en: AZUZZ: Most people think, oh, these guys just go out and burn whenever they want to.
cues.zh: AZUZZ：大多數人認為，哦，這些人只要想就出去燒死。

cues.text: God, I wish it was that easy AZUZZ: We go before the counties to get their permits.
cues.en: God, I wish it was that easy AZUZZ: We go before the counties to get their permits.
cues.zh: 天啊，我希望事情就是這麼簡單 AZUZZ：我們先到各縣去獲得許可。

cues.text: AZUZZ: We go before our tribal councils to get their permission and their permits to burn on tribal land.
cues.en: AZUZZ: We go before our tribal councils to get their permission and their permits to burn on tribal land.
cues.zh: AZUZZ：我們向部落委員會尋求許可，並獲得在部落土地上焚燒的許可。

cues.text: AZUZZ: We go before the tribal air quality.
cues.en: AZUZZ: We go before the tribal air quality.
cues.zh: AZUZZ：我們先考慮部落的空氣品質。

cues.text: AZUZZ: We go before the county's air quality.
cues.en: AZUZZ: We go before the county's air quality.
cues.zh: AZUZZ：我們首先考慮的是縣內的空氣品質。

cues.text: AZUZZ: And then I work with NOAA to predict my weather throughout that week while we're burning.
cues.en: AZUZZ: And then I work with NOAA to predict my weather throughout that week while we're burning.
cues.zh: AZUZZ：然後我與 NOAA 合作預測燃燒期間整個一週的天氣。

cues.text: AZUZZ: Once we have ignition, everybody falls in the place they need to be in.
cues.en: AZUZZ: Once we have ignition, everybody falls in the place they need to be in.
cues.zh: AZUZZ：一旦我們點火，每個人都會跌倒在他們需要的地方。

cues.text: AZUZZ: They have their tools ready, they have their radios on, we all know where everybody is at every moment.
cues.en: AZUZZ: They have their tools ready, they have their radios on, we all know where everybody is at every moment.
cues.zh: AZUZZ：他們準備好了工具，開啟了收音機，我們都知道每個人每時每刻都在哪裡。

cues.text: The fire started in these controlled burns moves slowly across the forest floor and clears
cues.en: The fire started in these controlled burns moves slowly across the forest floor and clears
cues.zh: 在這些受控制的燃燒中引發的火災緩慢地穿過森林地面並消失

cues.text: out the buildup of dead material.
cues.en: out the buildup of dead material.
cues.zh: 排除死物質的堆積。

cues.text: If the wind shifts, or fire gets too high it’s quickly contained and put out by the
cues.en: If the wind shifts, or fire gets too high it’s quickly contained and put out by the
cues.zh: 如果風向改變，或者火勢太高，它會很快被控制並被撲滅。

cues.text: trained crew.
cues.en: trained crew.
cues.zh: 訓練有素的船員。

cues.text: There's not one piece of our day that isn't choreographed.
cues.en: There's not one piece of our day that isn't choreographed.
cues.zh: 我們這一天的每一件事都是經過精心設計的。

cues.text: In 2020 and 2021 lawmakers introduced bills to increase the use of controlled burning nationwide.
cues.en: In 2020 and 2021 lawmakers introduced bills to increase the use of controlled burning nationwide.
cues.zh: 2020 年和 2021 年，立法者提出法案，增加全國控制燃燒的使用。

cues.text: It’s a start, but it’s won't be enough on it’s own.
cues.en: It’s a start, but it’s won't be enough on it’s own.
cues.zh: 這是一個開始，但光靠它還不夠。

cues.text: Recent data shows wildfires are only getting larger and more destructive year after year.
cues.en: Recent data shows wildfires are only getting larger and more destructive year after year.
cues.zh: 最近的資料顯示，野火規模逐年擴大，破壞性也越來越大。

cues.text: Campaigns like Smokey the Bear weren’t wrong to teach us to be careful with fire.
cues.en: Campaigns like Smokey the Bear weren’t wrong to teach us to be careful with fire.
cues.zh: 像斯莫基熊這樣的活動教導我們小心火災並沒有錯。

cues.text: Today, research shows that human carelessness like loose cigarettes, campfires, and sometimes
cues.en: Today, research shows that human carelessness like loose cigarettes, campfires, and sometimes
cues.zh: 如今，研究表明，人類的粗心行為，例如散落的香煙、篝火，有時甚至是

cues.text: even arson cause over 85% of disastrous wildfires.
cues.en: even arson cause over 85% of disastrous wildfires.
cues.zh: 85%以上的災難性野火甚至是縱火造成的。

cues.text: More controlled burns could help minimize those risks.
cues.en: More controlled burns could help minimize those risks.
cues.zh: 更受控制的燒傷有助於最大限度地減少這些風險。

cues.text: But we also need to recognize that fire is a natural part of the landscape we’re now
cues.en: But we also need to recognize that fire is a natural part of the landscape we’re now
cues.zh: 但我們也需要認識到，火是我們現在所處景觀的自然組成部分

cues.text: living in - and climate change is only going to make it worse.
cues.en: living in - and climate change is only going to make it worse.
cues.zh: 生活在－而氣候變遷只會讓情況變得更糟。

cues.text: That means building resilient communities and passing legislation that requires fire
cues.en: That means building resilient communities and passing legislation that requires fire
cues.zh: 這意味著建立有彈性的社群並透過需要火災的立法

cues.text: resistant materials in high-risk areas and truly educating the public on fire safety.
cues.en: resistant materials in high-risk areas and truly educating the public on fire safety.
cues.zh: 在高風險地區使用耐火材料，真正對民眾進行消防安全教育。

cues.text: AZUZZ: I..Yeah, saw Smokey Bear as a child and kind of thought that was going to
cues.en: AZUZZ: I..Yeah, saw Smokey Bear as a child and kind of thought that was going to
cues.zh: AZUZZ：我..是的，小時候看到史莫基熊，當時就想

cues.text: go in the wrong direction.
cues.en: go in the wrong direction.
cues.zh: 走錯方向了。

cues.text: But here I am as an adult, realizing that Smokey really frightened an entire population
cues.en: But here I am as an adult, realizing that Smokey really frightened an entire population
cues.zh: 但作為一個成年人，我意識到斯莫基確實嚇壞了所有人

cues.text: of people into realizing, if we do this, something's going to happen to us.
cues.en: of people into realizing, if we do this, something's going to happen to us.
cues.zh: 人們意識到，如果我們這樣做，就會發生一些事情。

cues.text: AZUZZL: We're going to lose our homes.
cues.en: AZUZZL: We're going to lose our homes.
cues.zh: AZUZZL：我們將失去家園。

cues.text: AZUZZ: We're going to destroy our environment.
cues.en: AZUZZ: We're going to destroy our environment.
cues.zh: AZUZZ：我們會破壞我們的環境。

cues.text: AZUZZ: Well, by not doing it, we're losing our homes and our environment is being destroyed.
cues.en: AZUZZ: Well, by not doing it, we're losing our homes and our environment is being destroyed.
cues.zh: 阿祖茲：嗯，如果不這麼做，我們就會失去家園，我們的環境就會被破壞。

cues.text: The Forest Service has a program called the Roots and Shoots program where
cues.en: The Forest Service has a program called the Roots and Shoots program where
cues.zh: 林務局有一個名為“根與芽”的計劃，其中

cues.text: they burn their grass for their basket weavers.
cues.en: they burn their grass for their basket weavers.
cues.zh: 他們為編織籃子的人燒草。

cues.text: Their grass is what gives us the white in our baskets and it's a serotinous plant — if it's not burned, it's not useable.
cues.en: Their grass is what gives us the white in our baskets and it's a serotinous plant — if it's not burned, it's not useable.
cues.zh: 它們的草給了我們籃子裡的白色，它是一種含血清的植物——如果不燒掉，它就無法使用。

cues.text: Our basket gathering sites are on a rotation, so every three to five years those are burned
cues.en: Our basket gathering sites are on a rotation, so every three to five years those are burned
cues.zh: 我們的籃子收集地點是輪換的，所以每三到五年就會被燒毀

cues.text: because for the first three years you can continue to gather hazel sticks in a certain site where it's been burned.
cues.en: because for the first three years you can continue to gather hazel sticks in a certain site where it's been burned.
cues.zh: 因為在最初的三年裡，你可以繼續在某個被燒毀的地方收集榛樹枝。

cues.text: Other plants don't require fire that often.
cues.en: Other plants don't require fire that often.
cues.zh: 其他植物並不經常需要火。
